review.reason: Primary study followed from a research briefing; separates corpus analysis from reader experiments.

item.title: Quantifying the prevalence and impact of overreaching causal claims in social science
item.headline: Causal wording changes how readers interpret correlational studies
item.authors: Calvin Isch, Timothy Dörr, Neil Fasching, Grace Jennings, Duncan J. Watts
item.summary: A corpus analysis found frequent causal wording in cross-sectional research. Separate reader experiments showed that phrasing affects interpretation. Classification and sampling constrain the prevalence estimate.

evidence.question: Does wording overstate causal evidence?
evidence.method: Validated text classification and reader experiments.
evidence.limitations: The selected corpus does not represent every study design.

explainer.finding: Causal language can strengthen readers’ causal interpretations.
explainer.method: Readers encountered original or associationally rewritten abstracts.
explainer.limits: Corpus prevalence depends on classification; experimental results concern the tested reading tasks.
